meta.title: Green space and walking among older adults

question.text: To what extent does the share of green space within 300 metres of home change self-reported walking among adults over 65 in Ghent?
question.tertium_comparationis: minutes of self-reported walking per week, compared between residents above and below the local green-space median
question.scope: Adults aged 65 and over in Ghent, 2026 to 2028, excluding residents of care homes.
question.completion_criterion: The question is answered when weekly walking minutes are estimated against green-space share with a model that adjusts for age, income and street connectivity, and the uncertainty of the estimate is reported.

method.approach: Cross-sectional comparison of neighbourhoods above and below the local green-space median, with individual-level controls.
sources: Neighbourhood green-space inventory, City of Ghent, 2025
Health survey of residents aged 65 and over, 2026-2028
Street network data, 2025, for connectivity measures
method.procedure: Draw a stratified sample of 1,200 residents across 60 neighbourhoods; measure green-space share within 300 metres of each home; collect walking minutes with a seven-day diary; estimate walking minutes against green-space share with neighbourhood random effects and individual controls; check for selective residential sorting with length of residence.
validity_conditions: Green-space share is measured on the same inventory for every neighbourhood
Walking is recorded in the same week of the year for all participants
Neighbourhoods above and below the median are similar in income and age structure
limits: The design is cross-sectional: it cannot separate green space from the people who choose to live near it
Self-reported walking overstates walking measured by accelerometry
Findings apply to a mid-sized European city, not to rural or metropolitan settings

results.claim: Residents above the green-space median report more weekly walking minutes, and the difference is larger among residents with lower incomes.
results.falsifier: Walking minutes do not differ between the two groups once age, income and connectivity are controlled, or the difference is smaller among lower-income residents.
results.evidence_needed: Seven-day walking diaries, green-space share per home, and the control variables for every participant.

results.claim: A neighbourhood-level green-space and walking dataset, with the code that builds it.
results.evidence_needed: The dataset and its build script, deposited with the project's data package.

warrant.gap_statement: Local green-space inventories and health surveys are collected by different agencies, so the association between green-space share and walking has not been estimated for Ghent.
evidence: WHO, Urban green spaces and health, 2016
